title: Sequential Pricing Rules with DO Block
prompt: You have a products table with columns product_id, category, base_price, and final_price (initially NULL). Write a DO block that applies pricing rules sequentially: (1) Set final_price to base_price for all rows. (2) Apply a 10% discount (multiply by 0.90) to Electronics category products. (3) Apply an additional $5 discount (subtract 5) to any product where final_price is now greater than 100. (4) Round all final_price values to 2 decimal places. After the DO block, write a SELECT statement that returns all columns ordered by product_id ascending. The output should show the final state of the products table after all transformations.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE products (product_id INT PRIMARY KEY, category VARCHAR(50), base_price DECIMAL(10,2), final_price DECIMAL(10,2));

hints: You need to write a DO block that performs multiple UPDATE statements in sequence, where each UPDATE builds on the results of the previous one.
Start by copying base_price to final_price, then apply the category discount, then check if the current final_price value exceeds the threshold for the additional discount.

Use UPDATE products SET final_price = base_price; then UPDATE products SET final_price = final_price * 0.90 WHERE category = 'Electronics'; then UPDATE products SET final_price = final_price - 5 WHERE final_price > 100; then UPDATE products SET final_price = ROUND(final_price, 2);
